messages.author: 516ff7247455fe07
messages.subject: MLR estimator output interpretation
parts:
To fit my model with likert scales I used the MLR estimator as suggested by literature. Looking at the results however, I am confused as to what result I use. For the chi-square statistics? Is it the 167.055? or the 207.107 ? and if so can anyone explain how this came about? Thank you very much. 





Optimization method                           NLMINB               
  Number of free parameters                         23               
                                                                     
  Number of observations                           104

  Model Fit Test Statistic                     207.107     167.055
  Degrees of freedom                                43          43
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000       0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                  1.240
    for the Yuan-Bentler correction (Mplus variant)

Model test baseline model:

  Minimum Function Test Statistic              502.329     369.713
  Degrees of freedom                                55          55
  P-value                                        0.000       0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                  1.359

messages.subject: Re: MLR estimator output interpretation
parts:
Yes, that p value would indicate that the specified model is not a good fit to the data. Car...@web.de's point is that some researchers would suggest that since chi-square is sensitive to sample size that you might consider other indexes of fit. But if you bring that up on SEMNET you get blasted by one particularly individual who will respond to you in all caps...

In the example given, with around 100 observations, that seems to be a pretty bad model fit.
